extracted.intended_audience: Harvard investigators, research administrators, and proposal preparers involved in NSF-funded off-campus or off-site research (faculty, postdocs, students, staff, and sponsored projects offices)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and institutional requirements for preparing the NSF-required Plan for Safe and Harassment-free Working Environments for any proposal involving off-campus or off-site research, plus related Harvard grants management and post-award responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to include NSF Safe and Harassment-free Working Environments plan
rubrics_metrics.description: All NSF proposals with any work considered off-campus or off-site must include a plan for ensuring the work environment is safe and harassment-free for all participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided Word template (linked); complete the boxes for your specific grant; your plan should not exceed two pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of off-campus or off-site research
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF defines off-campus or off-site research as data/information/samples being collected off-campus or off-site, such as fieldwork and research activities on vessels and aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether proposal activities meet this definition to determine if the NSF plan is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviors the plan must address
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan must describe how the following types of behavior will be addressed: abuse of any person (including, but not limited to, harassment, stalking, bullying, or hazing); and conduct that is unwelcome, offensive, indecent, obscene, or disorderly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains these are examples of misbehavior that undermine university mission and that the plan should describe responses if such behavior occurs while off-site research is conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for students and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring all students and employees (faculty and staff) complete campus-supported training addressing issues of sexual harassment and sexual violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specific online training is referenced (provost.harvard.edu/sexual-harassment-prevention-online-training); include evidence of training expectations/requirements in planning and preparation for off-site activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to University policies and incident reporting/resolution processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize Harvard University policies to address conduct expectations, including processes for how incident reports are made and how reports received are resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant policies to cite or align with include: University-Wide Statement on Rights and Responsibilities; Sexual Harassment and Other Sexual Misconduct Policy; Interim Title IX Sexual Harassment Policy; Interim Other Sexual Misconduct Policy; Non-discrimination and Anti-Bullying Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide resources to support healthy climate and prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans and programs should make resources available to help create a healthy climate and prevent hostile and intimidating behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of resources listed: Harvard University Options and Resources; Harvard University SHARE Counselors; Harvard University Health Services; Harvard University Counseling and Mental Health Services; Harvard University Office for Community Support, Non-Discrimination, Rights and Responsibilities; Report a Concern; Harvard University Police Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and document regularly scheduled prevention and fieldwork safety training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and document training sessions and workshops on Sexual Harassment, Discrimination Prevention, and Fieldwork Safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named offerings include: Preventing and Responding to Sexual Harassment and Other Sexual Misconduct; Cultivating a Climate of Gender Equity and Inclusion; Prevention Education; Fieldwork Safety and Best Practices Workshop (FAS). Include planned training in the NSF plan as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-departure support and international trip registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Harvard Global Support Services (GSS) for pre-departure support and international trip registration to enable SOS assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link provided to GSS travel/advice for sexual-assault and gender-violence support; include use of GSS processes and registration in off-site planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Sponsored Programs (OSP) role in award/post-award management
rubrics_metrics.description: Award management (post-award) is managed by the Office of Sponsored Programs (OSP) in close collaboration with school-based sponsored projects and research administration offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit OSP’s website for a complete overview of award management policies and procedures; OSP coordinates post-award requirements relating to expenditure of sponsored research funds and fiduciary responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: University oversight via Sponsored Administration Leadership Committee (SALC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harvard has three sponsored programs offices overseen collaboratively by the Sponsored Administration Leadership Committee (SALC), the Vice Provost for Research, and the University Director of Sponsored Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University-wide policies developed by SALC are available under the See Also section of the page or on OSP’s website — consult these for institution-wide grants management expectations and policy alignment.
